Challenge 1: The Facilitator

Your Task: Facilitate a 10 minute awareness session on the topic assigned to you.
Target Audience: Young people aged 15–18.

You will have 10 minutes to conduct your session.
You are free to choose your approach and format. Creativity and interactive methods are strongly encouraged; PowerPoint presentations are not permitted.
You may use any appropriate materials, resources, or activities to support your session.
Your session must actively engage the audience through interaction, discussion, questions, demonstrations, games, or other suitable methods.
You must communicate information accurately, clearly, and professionally.
Your session should have a clear objective and leave the audience with a meaningful takeaway.
NO AI
Remember: The goal is not simply to present information, but to facilitate an engaging awareness session that captures the audience’s attention and encourages participation.
You're Never Truly Alone: The World of Microbes
Explore the invisible organisms around us and the roles they play in everyday life.

CHALLENGE 2: THE CREATIVE CAMPAIGN

Your Task: Develop and present an original campaign addressing an assigned brief. Your goal is to design a campaign that motivates a specific audience to take action or adopt a desired behavior.
Target Audience: To be defined by the assigned campaign brief.

You must develop an original campaign concept that responds to the brief’s objective.
Your campaign should have a clear goal, a defined target audience, and a specific action or outcome you want to achieve.
You must explain your campaign’s main idea, key messages, communication methods, and planned activities.
You should demonstrate how you would engage your target audience and motivate them to participate or take action.
You must explain how the campaign could be implemented realistically, considering the available resources, and how its success could be measured.
You are free to choose your presentation format. Creative materials, mock-ups, posters, social media content, or other relevant resources are encouraged.
You have 10 minutes to present.
Remember: The goal is not simply to raise awareness or present an idea, but to develop a creative, realistic campaign that inspires action and achieves a meaningful result.
Recruitment Without the Recruitment Poster

Design a campaign to recruit 30 new Youth Sector volunteers aged 16–22. You cannot rely on ordinary recruitment posters or simply post an application link. Your campaign must make young people curious enough to take the first step.

CHALLENGE 3: THE CASE STUDY
Your Task: Analyze an assigned case study, identify the main problem or challenge, and propose a practical, well-reasoned solution.

You must analyze the situation, identify the key issues, and explain the factors contributing to the problem.
You must propose a clear and realistic solution, supported by logical reasoning.
You should outline how your proposed solution could be implemented, including the resources, steps, or collaboration required.
You must identify potential obstacles or risks and explain how you would address them.
You should explain how you would evaluate the success and effectiveness of your proposed solution.
You will have 10 minutes to present your analysis and proposed solution, followed by 2 minutes of questions from the evaluation committee.
You are free to choose your presentation format. Visual aids or other appropriate materials may be used to support your analysis.
Remember: The goal is not simply to describe the problem, but to demonstrate critical thinking, creativity, sound judgment, and the ability to develop a feasible solution.
The Declining Youth Sector

Attendance at Jbeil center has dropped significantly over six months. New members seem disengaged, activities attract fewer beneficiaries, and existing members are losing motivation.
Task: Identify the possible causes and develop a realistic plan to improve participation and retain members.

Challenge 4: Teach Us Something We Don’t Know
Your Task: Teach the evaluation committee a practical skill or concept of your choice within a short, interactive session.

You must  prepare a session that teaches the audience how to perform the skill in your assigned topic.
You are free to choose your teaching method. Demonstrations, hands-on activities, games, simulations, and other creative approaches are encouraged.
You must actively involve the audience and provide an opportunity for participants to practice the skill.
Your instructions must be clear, accurate, and easy to follow.
You must include a way to check whether the audience has learned or can apply the skill.
You may use any appropriate materials or resources to support your session.
You will have 10 minutes to conduct your session.
Remember: The goal is not simply to explain a skill, but to teach it effectively so that the audience can understand it and attempt to perform it themselves.

Challenge 5: Wearing Different Hats

Your Task: Develop and present a strategic plan outlining how you would contribute to the Lebanese Red Cross Youth Sector as an Executive Committee member.
Your presentation should demonstrate your understanding of the responsibilities of the Executive Committee, your vision for the center, and your ability to translate that vision into concrete actions.

You must identify the key responsibilities of an Executive Committee member and explain how you would approach the role.
You must present a clear vision for the center and identify its main priorities for development.
You must propose at least three concrete objectives you would work toward as an Executive Committee member.
For each objective, you must outline the actions you would take, how you would implement them, and the outcomes you expect to achieve.
You must explain how you would contribute to teamwork, decision-making, accountability, and collaboration within the Executive Committee.
You must demonstrate how your plan aligns with the values, mission, and regulations of the Lebanese Red Cross.
Your proposals must be realistic, achievable, and appropriate to the responsibilities and authority of an Executive Committee member.
You are free to choose your presentation format. Slides, timelines, action plans, or other visual materials may be used to communicate your ideas.
You have 10 minutes to present.
President

Develop and present a strategic plan outlining how you would contribute to the Lebanese Red Cross Youth Sector in the Executive Committee role of President. Apply all Challenge 5 requirements to this role.
